correctness.rationale: Maximum overlap degree one makes every connected term component a singleton or one edge, and different components act on disjoint qubit sets. The Pauli-mixture lemma is an explicit convex decomposition. For commuting pairs the nonidentity coefficient l1 norm is at most 2t+t^2<=1 exactly through t=sqrt2-1. For anticommuting pairs tanh(beta r)(|a|+|b|)/r<=2 beta J<1 at the same boundary, so they are safely separable. For H=-J(XX+ZZ), the partial-transpose Bell eigenvalue (1-2t-t^2)/4 changes sign exactly above t=sqrt2-1, proving sharpness. The packaged checker corroborates the scalar inequalities and witness sign transition.
risks: The theorem is for finite systems, coefficient cap |J_i|<=J, and the specified term-overlap graph.

originality.rationale: Fresh inspection of the primary 2026 paper confirms that its exact universal theorem, notation, tree recursion, and sharpness construction assume maximum overlap degree Delta>=2. Its weighted all-degree corollary yields only the weaker sufficient degree-one bound beta J<=1/(4e). Fresh Resultary and keyword searches found no universal Delta=1 theorem at atanh(sqrt2-1). The submitted result is therefore a genuine missing boundary case rather than a substitution into the published Delta>=2 formula.
